instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires expense statements by registered principals on or before July 31 and January 31, not an annual lobbyist-filed spending report.
No provision requires lobbyists to file monthly spending reports; periodic expense statements are filed by principals semiannually.
The only periodic spending report described is the principal’s expense statement; lobbyists only supply information to principals, so there is no other lobbyist-filed cadence.
The statute specifies semiannual filing dates (July 31 and January 31) for principal expense statements and does not create a quarterly lobbyist spending report.
Semiannual expense statements are filed by the principal, while the lobbyist only provides supporting information to the principal and signs that information.
Nothing in the provided subchapter requires tri-annual lobbyist spending reports; the only periodic report described is the principal’s semiannual statement.
Expense reporting is imposed on principals, and lobbyists are only required to furnish information for the principal’s statement, so there is no separate lobbyist itemization requirement.
Legislative proposals/topics must be reported by the principal as a condition of lobbying, not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.
Compensation to lobbyists is reported in the principal’s expense statement, and the lobbyist only supplies information to the principal rather than disclosing earnings in a lobbyist-filed report.
The principal’s expense statement requires time and expenditure information but does not require lobbyists to file or disclose contacts in a lobbyist spending report.
Per-issue time estimates are reported by the principal (topics accounting for 10% or more of time), not as lobbyist expenditure-per-issue disclosures.
Reporting of topics/legislative proposals is required of the principal to the commission, not of lobbyists in their own spending reports.
The statute’s activity-identification requirement applies to principals (reporting proposals/topics to the commission) rather than to lobbyists as separate filers.
The statute regulates gifts and other things of pecuniary value but does not require lobbyists to file a spending report itemizing such costs; expense statements are filed by principals.
Indirect lobbying costs are reported in the principal’s expense statement and supported by lobbyist-provided information, not by a lobbyist-filed periodic report.
The law does not require lobbyists to file their own spending reports (itemized or otherwise), instead requiring principals to file expense statements.
A lobbyist license application may include the address of the lobbyist’s primary residence, but there is no lobbyist-filed spending report requiring address/phone disclosures.
Identification of legislative proposals/topics is reported by principals to the commission; the statute does not require lobbyists to report bills/actions in their own periodic spending reports.
Disclosure of the principal’s business activity/nature is required in the principal’s registration statement, not in a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Principals file their own registration statements containing their business address; lobbyists are not required to file a spending report disclosing principal address/phone.

A lobbyist authorization for each principal must be filed with the commission, but this is not a lobbyist periodic spending report and does not impose a lobbyist spending-report duty to list all principals.
Legislative proposals/proposed administrative rule numbers must be reported by principals, not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.
Direct lobbying costs such as compensation to lobbyists are components of the principal’s expense statement; lobbyists do not file their own spending report disclosing compensation.
Aggregate total lobbying expenditures are reported by the principal in its expense statement, not by lobbyists in a separate periodic spending report.
Because lobbyists are not required to file any spending report (itemized or compensation) and principals are the required filers, the rubric question’s lobbyist-report requirement is not met.
The statute imposes periodic filing duties on principals, not on lobbyists, so it does not require a lobbyist to file a ‘no activity’ spending report.

While the statute contains an exception about furnishing things of value to a lobbyist’s relative/household member, it does not require lobbyists to file a report disclosing spending on household members of public officials; spending reports are filed by principals.
There is no lobbyist-filed spending report at all under these provisions, so there is no requirement that lobbyists disclose itemized information rather than aggregates.
